summary: This tutorial covers how to use JChemPaint, a chemical structures editor, on Ubuntu Linux OS version 12.04 with Java version 7. It starts by launching JChemPaint through the terminal using specific commands. The tutorial then moves on to exploring periodic table trends within JChemPaint. Users can select elements from the periodic table or type their symbols directly into the text box. The software displays detailed information about the selected element in a box. To create a molecule like xenon difluoride (XeF2), users navigate to the edit menu, set preferences to show implicit hydrogens, and draw bonds between atoms. The tutorial also explains how to change an element's isotopes and properties using the atom popup menu, demonstrating the transition from xenon to calcium as an example.
